title: Checkpoint: Perception and Attention
objective: After this level you can explain how perception and attention decide what you notice and what you miss.
summary: Attention is a limited resource that selects a little from a lot. Chapter 2 traced how sensations become perceptions, and how attention decides what you notice and what you miss.

cards.headline: Chapter 2 finale: you never take in everything.
cards.body: Your senses collect far more than you notice. This chapter has been about the filters: how the mind builds perceptions and how attention picks what makes it through. First, the oldest description of that filter; then the whole chapter on one timeline.

cards.headline: A little from a lot
cards.body: In 1890 William James wrote that attention "implies withdrawal from some things in order to deal effectively with others." Psychologists today describe that as limited capacity: you can attend to, or be aware of, only a small amount of information at a time. Every level in this chapter is a variation on that theme.

cards.headline: Perception and attention, in six studies

events.label: Wertheimer's still images that seem to move launch Gestalt psychology
Vicary's popcorn claim, later admitted to be made up
McGurk and MacDonald: lips change what you hear
Simons and Chabris: the invisible gorilla

cards.headline: From signal to experience
cards.body: Put the chapter together. Perception organizes and interprets sensations, merging the senses when they overlap, as the McGurk effect shows. Then attention selects. What it doesn't select can vanish, even in plain sight: that's inattentional blindness, and it catches experts too.

cards.headline: Chapter 2 complete
learned: How your mind turns raw sensations into perceptions by grouping them and filling in expectations.
Why you can miss a gorilla in plain sight, yet hear your own name across a noisy room.
Why switching between tasks costs time and accuracy, and why hands-free phones don't fix driving.
What hidden messages can and can't do, and how the famous popcorn claim fell apart.
